title: Thermodynamics
subject: Physics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Rapid Revision Deck

cards.q: State the Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics and its physical significance.
cards.a:
If systems A and B are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system C, then A and B are in thermal equilibrium with each other.
Physical significance: Introduces and defines the concept of TEMPERATURE as a state variable.
cards.hint: Two bodies in thermal equilibrium have the exact same temperature.

cards.q: State the First Law of Thermodynamics and its mathematical equation.
cards.a: dQ = dU + dW = dU + P · dV, where dQ is heat added to system, dU is change in internal energy, and dW is work done by system.
cards.hint: Based on the Universal Law of Conservation of Energy applied to thermodynamic systems.

cards.q: Sign conventions for dQ, dW, and dU in First Law of Thermodynamics?
cards.a:
dQ > 0: Heat absorbed by system; dQ < 0: Heat rejected by system.
dW > 0: Work done BY system (expansion, dV > 0); dW < 0: Work done ON system (compression, dV < 0).
dU > 0: Temperature increases (internal energy increases); dU < 0: Temperature decreases.
cards.hint: Always check whether work is done 'by' or 'on' the gas before choosing sign!

cards.q: Internal Energy U of an ideal gas depends on what?
cards.a: Internal energy of an ideal gas depends SOLELY on its absolute temperature T: dU = n C_v dT (independent of pressure or volume).
cards.hint: For an ideal gas undergoing any isothermal process (ΔT = 0), ΔU is ALWAYS 0.

cards.q: Work done in an Isothermal Process (T = constant)?
cards.a:
W = n R T ln(V₂ / V₁) = 2.303 n R T log₁₀(V₂ / V₁) = n R T ln(P₁ / P₂).
Since ΔT = 0 ⇒ ΔU = 0, heat absorbed equals work done: Q = W.
cards.hint: Carried out very slowly in conducting containers so system stays in thermal equilibrium.

cards.q: Work done in an Adiabatic Process (dQ = 0)?
cards.a:
W = [ P₁ V₁ - P₂ V₂ ] / (γ - 1) = [ n R (T₁ - T₂) ] / (γ - 1).
Since dQ = 0, First Law gives ΔU = - W.
cards.hint: If gas expands adiabatically (W > 0), ΔU < 0, so gas cools down (T₂ < T₁).

cards.q: Work done in an Isobaric Process (P = constant) and Isochoric Process (V = constant)?
cards.a:
Isobaric: W = P (V₂ - V₁) = n R (T₂ - T₁).
Isochoric: W = 0 (since dV = 0), so dQ = dU = n C_v dT.
cards.hint: In an isochoric process, 100% of the heat supplied goes entirely into increasing internal energy.

cards.q: Slope of Adiabatic vs Isothermal curve on a P-V indicator diagram?
cards.a:
Isothermal slope: (dP / dV)_iso = - P / V
Adiabatic slope: (dP / dV)_adi = - γ (P / V) = γ × (isothermal slope).
cards.hint: Because γ > 1, the adiabatic curve is always STEEPER than the isothermal curve by a factor of γ.

cards.q: Work done in a Cyclic Process on a P-V diagram?
cards.a:
W_net = Area enclosed by the closed P-V loop.
Clockwise loop: Net Work is POSITIVE (Heat Engine).
Counter-clockwise loop: Net Work is NEGATIVE (Refrigerator / Heat Pump).
cards.hint: In any complete cycle, initial and final states are identical, so ΔU_net = 0 and Q_net = W_net.

cards.q: Thermal Efficiency η of a Heat Engine?
cards.a: η = W / Q_H = (Q_H - Q_C) / Q_H = 1 - Q_C / Q_H, where Q_H is heat absorbed from hot reservoir and Q_C is heat rejected to cold reservoir.
cards.hint: η is always strictly less than 1 (100%) for any real or ideal heat engine.

cards.q: Efficiency of a Carnot Engine operating between T_H and T_C?
cards.a: η_Carnot = 1 - T_C / T_H = (T_H - T_C) / T_H.
cards.hint: T_H (source) and T_C (sink) MUST be in KELVIN! Carnot efficiency is the theoretical maximum.

cards.q: Four operations of the Carnot Cycle in order?
cards.a:
1. Isothermal Expansion at T_H (heat Q_H absorbed).
2. Adiabatic Expansion (temperature drops from T_H to T_C).
3. Isothermal Compression at T_C (heat Q_C rejected).
4. Adiabatic Compression (temperature rises from T_C to T_H).
cards.hint: Two reversible isothermals and two reversible adiabatics alternating.

cards.q: Coefficient of Performance β (or K) of a Refrigerator?
cards.a:
β = Q_C / W = Q_C / (Q_H - Q_C) = T_C / (T_H - T_C).
Relation with Carnot efficiency: β = (1 - η) / η.
cards.hint: Unlike efficiency η which is < 1, COP β can easily be greater than 1 (e.g. β = 4 or 5).

cards.q: MHT-CET Trap: If an open refrigerator is kept running inside a closed, insulated room, what happens to room temperature?
cards.a:
The room temperature INCREASES (room warms up)!
Because heat rejected to the room Q_H = Q_C + W is greater than heat absorbed Q_C by the amount of electrical work done W.
cards.hint: The motor's electrical energy is dissipated as extra heat into the closed room.

cards.q: Second Law of Thermodynamics: Kelvin-Planck and Clausius statements?
cards.a:
Kelvin-Planck: It is impossible to construct a heat engine whose sole effect is to extract heat from a reservoir and convert it 100% into work without rejecting heat (η < 1).
Clausius: It is impossible to transfer heat spontaneously from a cooler body to a hotter body without external work.
cards.hint: Both statements are logically equivalent and rule out 100% efficient engines and self-acting refrigerators.

cards.q: Fraction of heat converted into work in an Isobaric expansion of an ideal gas?
cards.a:
Fraction = W / Q = (C_p - C_v) / C_p = 1 - 1 / γ.
For monoatomic (γ = 5/3): W/Q = 1 - 3/5 = 2/5 (40%).
For diatomic (γ = 7/5): W/Q = 1 - 5/7 = 2/7 (28.6%).
cards.hint: Remaining heat goes into increasing internal energy: ΔU / Q = 1 / γ.

cards.q: A Carnot engine has efficiency 40% with sink at 300 K. What is the source temperature? To increase efficiency to 50%, what should source temperature be?
cards.hint: Standard 2-mark HSC numerical. Always keep temperatures in Kelvin.

cards.q: Reversible vs Irreversible Processes?
cards.a:
Reversible: Can be retracted in opposite direction through exact same intermediate equilibrium states without leaving any change in universe (quasi-static, no friction).
Irreversible: Cannot retrace path exactly (spontaneous, dissipative effects like friction, turbulence, rapid expansion).
cards.hint: All natural physical processes in the universe are irreversible.

cards.q: Free Expansion of an ideal gas into a vacuum: Values of dW, dQ, and dU?
cards.a:
dW = 0 (no opposing external pressure, P_ext = 0)
dQ = 0 (insulated container)
dU = 0 ⇒ ΔT = 0 (temperature remains constant).
cards.hint: Highly irreversible adiabatic process where no work is done and temperature does not change.

cards.q: For the same expansion from V₁ to V₂, which process has the maximum work done: Isothermal, Isobaric, or Adiabatic?
cards.a:
W_isobaric > W_isothermal > W_adiabatic.
Area under P-V curve is largest for isobaric and smallest for adiabatic.
cards.hint: During expansion, isobaric curve is highest, followed by isothermal, then adiabatic.

cards.q: For the same compression from V₁ to V₂ (V₂ < V₁), which process requires maximum work done?
cards.a:
W_adiabatic > W_isothermal > W_isobaric.
Adiabatic compression curve rises steepest, so area under it is the largest.
cards.hint: Reverse of expansion! More work must be supplied to compress adiabatically.

cards.q: What is a Quasi-static Process?
cards.a: An infinitely slow process in which the system remains in thermodynamic equilibrium with its surroundings at every intermediate instant.
cards.hint: Idealization required to trace well-defined paths on a P-V diagram.

cards.q: Work done by an expanding gas when pressure varies as P = a V + b?
cards.a:
W = ∫ P dV = ∫ (a V + b) dV = (a / 2) (V₂² - V₁²) + b (V₂ - V₁).
Geometrically: Area of trapezium under the straight line P-V graph = (1/2)(P₁ + P₂)(V₂ - V₁).
cards.hint: Use area of trapezium formula directly for linear P-V variations to save integration time!

cards.q: Heat capacity of an ideal gas during a polytropic process P V^x = constant?
cards.hint: For isothermal: x = 1 ⇒ C = ∞; for adiabatic: x = γ ⇒ C = 0; for isobaric: x = 0 ⇒ C = C_p.

cards.q: MHT-CET Trap: Can the specific heat capacity of a gas be negative?
cards.a: YES. During a process where heat is rejected (dQ < 0) while temperature rises due to strong compression, or when gas expands and cools while heat is added (e.g. polytropic process with 1 < x < γ), specific heat capacity C is NEGATIVE.
cards.hint: Unlike solids and liquids, a gas can have any specific heat capacity from -∞ to +∞!
